assessment.report:
# Role invocation: scoped development readiness

The user approved explicit named-role selection, availability checks, no silent generic fallback, and traceable actual subagent output. Existing role-routing, execution/ownership templates and architecture were inspected; no structural refactor, new orchestration runtime, PRD or OpenSpec adoption is required. Lead owns shared Skill/validator edits; a explicitly selected named Tester owns isolated tests and stage packet. A named Reviewer will assess the completed instructions.

This review addresses this bounded correction, not whole-project sufficiency or user acceptance. Other capability docs remain in place and are not declared re-certified or obsolete. No new requirement ambiguity blocks this scope.

The current session exposes named Tester/Reviewer role definitions with older GPT-6 Sol profiles than the source's GPT-6.1 Sol profiles. This is disclosed environment evidence, not an authorized replacement or a model upgrade. The role-selection checks can use those currently exposed named roles without altering configuration; resolved inference model identity may be unknown. Verifying the source model allocation requires a separate authorized installation/fresh-session check and remains unverified.

Before main implementation, the Tester prepares/validates the stage packet and observes an actual package-route regression Red. At close, review changed sources and new packet information, record a fresh assessment, preserve prior system-owned records and leave user-only acceptance pending. Skill constraints and authored records are reviewable workflow requirements, not an unbypassable runtime gate or proof of identity/approval.
